A_target.statement:
Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be [[Definition:Continuous Real Function|continuous]] functions on $S \subseteq \R$ converging [[Definition:Uniform Convergence|uniformly]] to $f$.
Then $f$ is continuous.

B_source.statement: To prove $\map d {a, c} < \epsilon$, route through intermediate points $b_1, b_2$ with each of $\map d {a, b_1}$, $\map d {b_1, b_2}$, $\map d {b_2, c}$ less than $\dfrac \epsilon 3$, and apply the [[Triangle Inequality]].

substitutions.the three small distances: uniform closeness at x, continuity of f_N, uniform closeness at x_0

object_map.reformulation: Approximate f by a single continuous f_N and split the error into three thirds.

validity_conditions: Convergence must be uniform, so that one N works at both x and x_0.
Pointwise convergence alone does not suffice, as x^n on [0, 1] shows.
proof_plan:
Let $x_0 \in S$ and $\epsilon > 0$.
By uniform convergence, choose $N$ with $\size {\map {f_N} x - \map f x} < \dfrac \epsilon 3$ for all $x \in S$.
By continuity of $f_N$, choose $\delta > 0$ with $\size {x - x_0} < \delta \implies \size {\map {f_N} x - \map {f_N} {x_0} } < \dfrac \epsilon 3$.

For $\size {x - x_0} < \delta$, by the [[Triangle Inequality]]:
:$\size {\map f x - \map f {x_0} } \le \size {\map f x - \map {f_N} x} + \size {\map {f_N} x - \map {f_N} {x_0} } + \size {\map {f_N} {x_0} - \map f {x_0} } < \epsilon$

Hence $f$ is continuous at $x_0$, which is the [[Uniform Limit Theorem]].
{{qed}}
